problem: The new abandonment rule (stale marker regardless of pid, OR dead pid AND marker older than two heartbeats, else unmarked-and-old) is packed into one nested ternary with a mixed ||/&& clause and an unnamed `2 * heartbeatMs` grace multiplier. The 'two heartbeats' grace is a business rule that the docstring, review.ts help text and three docs restate in prose, but the code has no name for it.
impact: The next editor of the sweep, the one place that decides to delete directories, has to decode operator precedence and a bare multiplier to see which case applies. Changing the grace means finding the literal here and the prose copies elsewhere.
quote: : now() - owner.mtimeMs > staleHeartbeatMs || (!isAlive(owner.pid) && now() - owner.mtimeMs > 2 * heartbeatMs);

problem: findReviewGateState takes a fifth positional parameter, `now`, after the optional `signal`. Every new test call has to pass an `undefined` placeholder for the signal, e.g. `findReviewGateState(root, 0, {}, undefined, now)` (completion-gate.test.ts:749 and about ten other call sites). The internal SignatureOptions already moved to an options object for `now`, but the public function did not.
impact: Call sites read as `(root, 0, {}, undefined, now)`, so a reader has to open the signature to decode them, and adding the next injectable makes the list longer again.

problem: The new Swept line says the copies were 'left by dead passes'. The sweep it reports also removes directories whose pid is still alive but whose marker went stale (reused pid or another PID namespace), and unmarked directories older than six hours. The record field it renders is documented as 'dead or abandoned earlier passes', so the same concept has two names and the rendered text is the narrower, inaccurate one.
impact: An operator reading mutation-<n>.md after a sweep of a live-pid/stale-marker directory is told that a dead pass was cleaned up, which is not what happened.

problem: runMutation, already about 140 lines, now also owns the sweep orchestration across two bases with its own timing, the owner-marker heartbeat lifecycle (setInterval/unref, cleared in both the signal cleanup and the finally), and a new optional option. Provenance, sweep, scratch and marker setup, heartbeat, copy, baseline and mutant loop all sit at different abstraction levels in one body (SRP / single level of abstraction).
impact: Each new concern in the pass grows the same function. The heartbeat has to be cleared in two places, so the next person to add a teardown step has to find both.

problem: Three new tests (TP-004 and both LOGIC-003 tests) each build the same AbortController plus a `reviewGateState` stub that aborts and then returns openReview(). openReview was extracted as a helper, but the abort-then-resolve stub around it was pasted three times.
impact: A change to how the abort-during-gate scenario is staged has to be made in three places to keep the tests describing the same condition.

impact: A reader has to guess what 'base copy' refers to. It is low cost, but the rest of the docstring is precise.
